topic: STARTING OVER: a 15-minute Can-Wait List on one sheet of paper, parking money questions that do not need an answer this week and giving each a look-again date
pillar: STARTING OVER: the feelings and the small first moves (the 2 A.M. math, 'where did the money go, not why', permission to go slowly).
caption:
Some money questions can sit on a shelf for a while.
Take one sheet of paper and 15 minutes.
Write down every money question in your head, then circle the one or two that need an answer in the next seven days.
Give the rest a look-again date and let the paper hold them.
Save this for the next night your head feels crowded.

slides.title: The money decisions that can wait
slides.subtitle: A 15-minute Can-Wait List

slides.title: Your head is holding too many questions
slides.body: Sell the car? Move? Change banks? When every question feels urgent, it gets hard to answer any of them. A short list on paper can hold them for you.

slides.title: Make your Can-Wait List
items: Grab one sheet of paper and a pen. Set a 15-minute timer.
Write every money question that has been circling your head.
Next to each one, ask: does this need an answer in the next 7 days?
Circle the one or two that do. Everything else can wait.

slides.title: Give each one a look-again date
slides.body: Next to every item you did not circle, write a date. Maybe two weeks out. Maybe after the holidays. The question has a home now, and you can set it down.

slides.title: What often ends up on the list
items: Whether to keep or sell the house or the car
Big changes to retirement or savings accounts
Moving banks or opening new accounts
Any big purchase you feel rushed to make this weekend

slides.title: Mark the questions that need a helper
slides.body: For settlement, tax or legal questions, write the word ask next to it. A licensed professional can help with the details when that date comes around.

slides.title: Tape it somewhere you will see it
slides.body: The fridge door works. When a question pops up at night, add it to the list and go back to bed. The two circled items are your only money jobs this week.

slides.title: Save this for your next busy-head night
